retryPolicy.reasonsHint: Comma or newline separated reason codes. Leave empty to use backend defaults.

loginUi.intro: If the app is already signed in, this step is skipped. Otherwise, it uses the account assigned to the phone.

loginUi.applicationLabel: Which application should be signed in?

leaseTarget.sourceHint: Each run takes one target this account has not processed; concurrent executions cannot reserve the same target.
leaseTarget.connectionHint: Takes a ready connection candidate and locks it for the account currently running.

adbShell.hint: Runs on the real phone — enter the full command (e.g. adb shell getprop …) or shell-only (getprop …).
adbShell.failOnErrorDescription: If disabled, non-zero exit still records output and the scenario continues.

scrollDown.intro: Swipe down to load more content (feed, lists…). Usually adjust repeat count and horizontal position — keep other defaults.
scrollDown.pauseHint: Wait for the UI to settle before the next swipe.
scrollDown.gestureHint: Ratio of screen height: 0 = top, 1 = bottom. Scroll down = start Y greater than end Y (e.g. 0.65 → 0.47).
scrollDown.directionDownOk: Direction OK: finger moves up on screen (content scrolls down).
scrollDown.directionWarning: Start Y is less than end Y — looks like swipe up, not feed scroll down.
scrollDown.anchorHint: Facebook feed: swipe near left/right edge to avoid full-width photos in the center. Use {varToken} if your campaign defines it.
scrollDown.durationHint: Short (~300–500 ms) feels natural; increase on slow devices.

selector.autoFillHint: Use “Pick from screen” or recording — class, app, and match rules are filled automatically. You usually only edit the main value (text, id…).
selector.byDescriptionHint: Matches the Android widget’s hidden content-desc label (screen-reader text), not necessarily what you see on screen. Facebook often puts group name + status here (e.g. “Claude VN, Public · 315K”). If the step fails, try “Visible text” instead.
selector.clickableDescription: Android clickable=true — enable when you need a real button/link, not static label text. Auto-set when picking a tappable node from the screen.
selector.advancedIntro: Most steps only need “Match by” and “Value” above. Open this when the tap misses, several similar elements exist, or you want to review auto-filled filters from screen pick.
selector.technicalDetailsHint: Only edit if you know Android UI structure. Usually leave as filled by screen pick.
selector.chainBlockHint: Use when the main element is only a label and the real control is inside or next to it (often set by recording).
selector.classNameHint: Extra Android view class filter — usually leave as filled by pick.
selector.fallbackHint: Tap at screen ratio (0–1) when the selector above does not find an element.

extract.intro: Read on-screen content, optionally expand “See more”, scroll to load more, then store in a variable or save to a collection.
extract.strategyGroupsDesc: Read group search results into the reusable source catalog.
extract.extractProfileHint: Balanced fits most FB groups. Aggressive scans deeper; Safe is faster and lighter.
extract.openPostBeforeExtractDescription: Tap timestamp/header to open the full post before parsing — recommended for FB group feeds.
extract.openPostPressBackDescription: Return to the feed right after extract. For comments, Back only runs when the agent still recognizes the comment sheet.
extract.openPostManualBackHint: Auto-back is off — add a Back step after extract when the scenario must return to the feed itself.
extract.expandSeeMoreDescription: Tap “See more” and wait for UI to settle before parsing — recommended for Facebook posts.
extract.stopIfNoNewDescription: Stop after several rounds with no new items — saves time.
extract.advancedExpandHint: Only adjust if content is still truncated or runs are too slow. Most FB campaigns keep defaults.
extract.edgeExtraDataDescription: Send hierarchy XML to the control host for more accurate Facebook post/comment parsing.
extract.strategyVersionHint: Only v1 is supported for now.
